column1: # Containers as DATA: what the step loop evaluates, and what it leaves
# alone. The bracket forms are documented in core/spec/README.md — `[ … ]`
# and `{ … }` are the PARSER's containers (Eval set), `[q … ]` and
# `{q … }` the runtime's, and `p( … )` is a paren-EXPRESSION value rather
# The eval/no-eval split is the whole subject, and writing these rows found
# two defects in core/ts. It descended into a map REGARDLESS of the Eval
# flag, so a map a word handler returned had its values evaluated on one
# side and not the other — `{q a: [ boomq 1 ] }` RAISED in TS where Go
# returned the map untouched. And a map value that evaluated to NOTHING
# kept its key as an empty list where Go drops the key entirely.
# --- the Eval flag decides, for lists and maps alike -----------------------
# A container the PARSER built evaluates its contents once, at the end of
# the run; one a word handler returned is data and stays verbatim. Quoting
# the OUTER container stops the descent — the inner one is not reached, so
# its own flag never gets a say.
# --- an error inside a container propagates — but only if reached ----------
